To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the social construction of the self is a process which takes place through the negotiation of intersubjective meanings and the performance of identity work, and that transgender identities, practices and subjectivities are constructed, negotiated and performed within the contexts of social and cultural discourses and the lived experiences of trans individuals, their families and friends.
the participants in our study described their experiences in terms of the social constructionist theory of the gendered self, which is a process of becoming and a process of being.

the participants in our study had experienced a variety of social and cultural influences that shaped their identities as trans people; they had been influenced by the wider culture, by the social and cultural context in which they had lived and by the people they had encountered in their lives; their gender variant identities had developed over a long period of time, in response to the influences of the people and the culture around them, and to the ways they had responded to those influences; their identities had been influenced by their experiences
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of gendered subjectivity in the social context.
the construction of identities, the reclaiming of subjectivities and the reconstruction of selves.
the ways in which gender variant individuals construct and reconstruct their identities, subjectivities and selves, through a range of practices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
transgender identities and practices are socially constructed and are therefore open to change.

transgender identities are constructed through a process of social interaction in which gendered meanings are negotiated and contested, with the aim of achieving a sense of coherence, and a degree of acceptance.
the findings of this thesis demonstrate the importance of social and historical context to an understanding of transgender identities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
transgender people have been able to construct identities and practices which are not necessarily congruent with those of the wider society.

the research findings suggest a complex and diverse range of gender variant identities and practices in the Scottish context, which have emerged and developed over time, in response to a range of social and historical influences.

we found the participants to be a group of people who have had to construct their gender identities in the face of social disapproval and who, in doing so, have had to negotiate the social construction of their gender identities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transgender people in Scotland, like transgender people elsewhere, are a diverse and heterogeneous group of people.

the transgender subject is not a fixed, essentialised entity, but a fluid and contingent identity that is constantly being constructed and reconstructed through the intersubjective interactions between the transgender subject, other transgender people, and non-transgender people.
the social construction of identity is an ongoing process, which involves the continual reworking of self-identity in relation to the social world.
